title: A Shared Birthday
problem: Assume 365 equally likely birthdays and no leap day. What is the probability that at least two people in a group of 23 share a birthday?

hints.text: Compute the complement that all 23 birthdays are distinct.

solution.setup: It is easier to calculate the probability of no shared birthday.
solution.reasoning: For the first person there is no restriction. Each subsequent birthday must avoid those already used, giving P(no match)=product from k=0 to 22 of (365-k)/365. Numerically this is about 0.492703. Subtracting from one gives about 0.507297.
solution.sanityCheck: There are C(23,2)=253 pairs, enough that a collision becomes plausible despite 365 possible days.

keyInsight: For at-least-one collision events, the no-collision complement has a clean sequential product.
recognitionCues: An at-least-one match among many pairs often becomes tractable through the all-distinct complement.
commonMistakes: Approximating the probability as 23/365 and ignoring the 253 possible pairs.
followUps: Use exp[-n(n-1)/(2·365)] to estimate the threshold group size for 50%.

source.notes: Original wording of the classical birthday problem.
